hints: A graph of $y=|2x+3|$ is formed by reflecting any part of $y=2x+3$ below the $x$-axis upwards.
Locate the vertex by solving $2x+3=0$, then draw the two straight-line branches meeting there.
walkthrough:
Find the $x$-intercept (vertex) of the modulus function where $2x + 3 = 0$:
$$2x + 3 = 0 \implies x = -\dfrac{3}{2} = -1.5$$
Thus, the vertex is at $(-1.5, 0)$.

Find the $y$-intercept by setting $x = 0$:
$$y = |2(0) + 3| = |3| = 3$$
Thus, the $y$-intercept is at $(0, 3)$.

Identify the two linear branches:
For $x \geqslant -1.5$: $y = 2x + 3$ (a straight line with positive gradient $2$).
For $x < -1.5$: $y = -(2x + 3) = -2x - 3$ (a straight line with negative gradient $-2$).

Draw the complete graph:
A symmetrical V-shaped graph with vertex on the $x$-axis at $(-1.5, 0)$, passing through $(0, 3)$ and $(-3, 3)$.

hints: Treat the modulus in cases, with $|2x+3|=2x+3$ or $-(2x+3)$ according to the sign of $2x+3$.
Solve $3x+8>|2x+3|$ on each relevant case interval and combine the valid values.
Keep the endpoint strict because the original inequality is $>$, not $\geq$.
walkthrough:
Consider the two algebraic cases determined by the sign of $(2x + 3)$:
$$|2x + 3| = \begin{cases} 2x + 3, & \text{if } x \geqslant -1.5 \\ -(2x + 3), & \text{if } x < -1.5 \end{cases}$$

Solve Case 1 where $x \geqslant -1.5$:
$$3x + 8 > 2x + 3$$
$$3x - 2x > 3 - 8$$
$$x > -5$$
Since $x \geqslant -1.5$, this entire region $x \geqslant -1.5$ satisfies the inequality.

Combine the two cases over the real number line:
For $x < -1.5$, we have $-2.2 < x < -1.5$.
For $x \geqslant -1.5$, we have $x \geqslant -1.5$.
The continuous union of these intervals gives:
$$x > -\dfrac{11}{5} \quad (\text{or } x > -2.2)$$
